text.p: Here is a chronology of key steps leading to the agreement on Hebron since Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation signed their peace accord on the White House lawn on September 13, 1993.
May 4, 1994 - Israel and PLO sign accord giving Palestinians in Gaza and Jericho the first self-rule since 1967 Middle East war.
May 11 - Israel begins transfer of power to PLO, hands over Gaza Strip military base to Palestinian police officers.
May 13 - Israel hands over Jericho in West Bank.
Sept 28, 1995 - Israel and PLO agree to extend self-rule to much of West Bank. Accord, nearly 16 months behind schedule, calls for Israeli troops to begin leaving Arab towns in 10 days.
Nov 13 - Israel begins redeployment from seven West Bank towns, handing over Jenin to PLO.
Dec 10 - Israel hands over Tulkarm, the second town.
Dec 11 - Israel hands over Nablus ahead of schedule.
Dec 16 - Israel hands over Qalqilya, closest town to its border with West Bank.
Dec 21 - Israel hands over Bethlehem, traditional birthplace of Jesus, just before Christmas.
March 23, 1996 - Israel, rocked by Islamic suicide bombings, puts off scheduled withdrawal from Hebron, the seventh town.
Jan 15, 1997 - Deal signed for Israeli redeployment in Hebron and setting dates for further three-stage pullback from most of West Bank by mid-1998.
